title: Remedies in tort — damages and injunction

content.overview: The primary tort remedy is unliquidated damages (compensatory; aggravated or exemplary in limited cases). Injunctions restrain continuing or threatened wrongs. Self-help is narrowly confined. Special statutes may fix structured compensation (e.g. motor accidents).

sections.heading: Damages
sections.body: Compensatory damages restore, so far as money can, the position as if the tort had not occurred — special (pecuniary) and general (non-pecuniary) heads. Remoteness limits recovery. Exemplary damages punish and deter in constrained categories; do not plead them as of course.

sections.heading: Injunction
sections.body: Prohibitory or mandatory injunctions where damages are inadequate — typical in nuisance and trespass. Interim injunctions require a serious question to be tried, balance of convenience, and irreparable injury analysis.

sections.heading: Track B
sections.body: Prayer must match the wrong: money, restraint, declaration, or statutory compensation route. Quantify special damages with documents. For MACT/consumer claims, use the statutory forum and schedule where applicable.
